spec.title: precisedelta() keeps the sign of a negative timedelta

placement: one machine: git worktree, native sandbox (bubblewrap), no microVM

reasons: Regression: precisedelta(datetime) now raises TypeError (worked on base, returned '1 hour')
Sub-unit negative values render as signed zero, e.g. '-0 seconds' / '-0 minutes'
Tests lack datetime and round-to-zero negative cases, so the regression went unnoticed
Sign check is fragile and redundant with _date_and_delta; uses a redundant local import

sessions.result:
`precisedelta()` now keeps the sign of a negative value, so `precisedelta(timedelta(seconds=-3661))` returns `'-1 hour, 1 minute and 1 second'`. The full suite passes (757 passed, 112 skipped), and `ruff check` is clean. I never ran the new tests against the base commit, so I haven't confirmed they fail without the fix.

- **The fix:** in `src/humanize/time.py`, `precisedelta()` reads the sign from the original value, whether a `timedelta` or a number of seconds. It puts a `-` in front of the result. The rule applies for any `minimum_unit`, `suppress` and `format`. Zero and positive values ren

I recommend rejecting this change. All 757 tests pass, but the change breaks input that worked before and adds behaviour the spec did not ask for.

1. **It breaks `datetime` input.** The new sign check (`seconds = value.total_seconds() if isinstance(value, dt.timedelta) else value`, then `seconds < 0`) assumes anything that isn't a `timedelta` is a number. `precisedelta()` has always accepted a `datetime`, because `_date_and_delta()` handles that case.
